general.reason: The paper explicitly states in Fig. 4's caption: "t-SNE visualisation of ViT-B/16 feature distributions across datasets," yet the main model uses ViT-H (~636M params). The paper provides no t-SNE or other feature-space analysis using the actual ViT-H backbone, so the OoD partition justification is based on a different, smaller model's feature space, not the one actually used in XCT-SAM.

evidence.claim: The t-SNE plot used to justify benchmark splits is computed on ViT-B/16, not the ViT-H backbone used in the main experiments, so the OoD partition justification is not assured for the model's actual feature space.
evidence.excerpt: Section IV.A relies on Fig. 4 to justify using Test-3 as validation and Test-1/2/4-6 (plus NIST) as OoD benchmarks, but the caption states "t-SNE visualisation of **ViT-B/16** feature distributions across datasets." The rest of the paper uses SAM ViT-H (~636M params). Feature clusters at ViT-B/16 are not the same object as the feature space the adapter actually shifts; whether Test-1/2/4-6 and NIST form OoD clusters *in the ViT-H representation the model uses* is not shown.

judge_panel.reason: The paper explicitly states in Fig. 4's caption: "t-SNE visualisation of ViT-B/16 feature distributions across datasets," yet the main model uses ViT-H (~636M params). The paper provides no t-SNE or other feature-space analysis using the actual ViT-H backbone, so the OoD partition justification is based on a different, smaller model's feature space, not the one actually used in XCT-SAM.

The paper explicitly uses Fig. 4 to justify the split — “As shown in Fig. 4, Train-1, Train-2, and Test-3 cluster closely ... motivating the use of Test-3 as the validation set” — but the figure is captioned “t-SNE visualisation of ViT-B/16 feature distributions across datasets,” while the main model “builds upon a SAM backbone based on the ViT-H image encoder.” The paper does not provide a corresponding ViT-H feature-space analysis or explain why the ViT-B/16 clustering should transfer to ViT-H.

The paper explicitly states in the caption of Fig. 4 that it shows a 't-SNE visualisation of ViT-B/16 feature distributions', despite previously stating in Section III.A that 'Our approach builds upon a SAM backbone based on the ViT-H image encoder', confirming the reviewer's claim.
